title: Primary-Loss Surcharge on Excess Flood Limit Increases
content:
A limit increase on an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** policy carries a surcharge where the primary flood policy beneath it has paid a claim recently.

## Clause

The primary-loss surcharge on an increase is 20 percent where the latest claim payment on the claim file of the Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy in force whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the policy record was issued fewer than 12 whole months before the increase is signed, 10 percent where it was issued at least 12 but fewer than 36 whole months before, and nothing otherwise or where that policy carries no claim payment.

The NFIP policy read is the Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)) in force whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record. Any claim payment on its claim file counts, whatever the coverage paid. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

Every surcharge percentage set on an increase is added into one increase loading, which acts once on the added limit's charge at the layer rate: that charge is multiplied by one plus the increase loading.

## Schedule

| Latest claim payment on that NFIP policy's claim file, whole months before the increase is signed | Primary-loss surcharge |
|---|---|
| 0 to 11 | 20 percent |
| 12 to 35 | 10 percent |
| 36 or more, or no claim payment | nothing |

## Boundaries (hypothetical)

For an increase signed on the 10th of a month: a latest payment issued on the 11th of the same month one year earlier is 11 whole months back (20 percent); one issued on the 10th is 12 whole months back (10 percent). Three years back, a payment on the 11th is 35 whole months (10 percent) and one on the 10th is 36 (nothing).
